The trick in multi-threading is to only lock things that can't fail. And one thing that can't fail is when you copy only memory as fast as possible as one big block of memory.

You:

  • Prepare the data.
  • Lock, memory copy, unlock.
  • Extract the data.

You also must realize that you can initialize data before you actually start to run the thread.

  • Prepare the thread
  • Copy the data
  • Start the thread.

Not every single variable needs to contain locking, only those that gets exposed to other threads.

[meta] Sorry for my absence! Let's make a community list of rules/requirements for posting in this sub. Please leave suggestions in comments :)

Obviously, every post needs to relate to the mods of Minecraft since there is already a v/minecraft where general Minecraft stuff can go. For instance, I don't think a post about someone making a super sweet building would be appropriate but if someone made a post about a super sweet factory set up they have I would love to see that here (especially since I noticed that there are a few techies in this subverse). Of course, this opens up a bit of a grey area where someone could show off their builds where the mods are part of the built but may not be the focus so I am not sure what to make of that.

I also remember reading the welcome post and more specifically the part that mentioned posting direct links. I really like this idea since Adfly is very annoying and most mods have direct links or mirrors.

There are also a significant amount of youtube channels that review/promote mods but I don't want to see posts where majority of the content is left for the viewer to follow a youtube link. For example, if a post comprised of the message: "hey all, I found this sweet mod and you should totally hit this youtube link for more info" then I would not like that. However, if someone goes into a lot of depth in their own narrative about the mod and supplies a wiki/youtube video at the end of their post for more information then I would be perfectly fine with that.

Pretty much, I just want this subverse to have quality content that relates/focuses on the modding aspect of Minecraft
